name: Generalized Systematic Review Registration
citation: van den Akker OR, Peters GJY, Bakker CJ, et al. Increasing the transparency of systematic reviews: presenting a generalized registration form. Syst Rev 2023;12:170.

items.label: Title
items.hint: Title of the review as it should appear in the registry. The review type belongs in the title.

items.label: Contributors
items.hint: Everyone who is listed as an author. OSF enters people with an OSF account here.

items.label: Subjects
items.hint: Subjects from OSF’s list, so that the registration can be found.

items.label: Tasks and roles
items.hint: Who takes on which task, for example search, screening, extraction, resolution, writing?

items.label: Type of review
items.hint: Review type and the guideline the approach follows; also the reporting standard.

items.label: Steps of the review
items.hint: The planned steps in their order.

items.label: Current status
items.hint: What has already happened at the time of registration? State it honestly, including trial runs of the search or a pilot that has begun.

items.label: Start
items.hint: Day on which the review starts or started.

items.label: End
items.hint: Planned completion of the review.

items.label: Background
items.hint: Why is this review needed? State of knowledge, gap and benefit in a few paragraphs.

items.label: Primary research question
items.hint: The question or questions the review is meant to answer.

items.label: Secondary research questions
items.hint: Subordinate questions; leave empty or enter “none” if there are none.

items.label: Expectations or hypotheses
items.hint: What does the team expect? For scoping reviews often “no hypotheses”; then give the reason.

items.label: Dependent variables, outcomes, main characteristics
items.hint: What is looked at in the sources? For scoping reviews the concept, for questions of effectiveness the outcomes.

items.label: Independent variables, interventions
items.hint: Interventions or exposures. Enter “not applicable” if the question has none.

items.label: Additional variables, covariates
items.hint: Further characteristics used in the analysis, such as setting, year or source type.

items.label: Software
items.hint: Programs for reference management, screening, extraction and analysis, with version.

items.label: Funding
items.hint: Funders and grant numbers, or “no funding”.

items.label: Conflicts of interest
items.hint: Conflicts of interest of those involved, or “none”.

items.label: Own work among the sources
items.hint: Could work by those involved be among the records? How is this handled, for example who does not screen it themselves?

items.label: Databases
items.hint: All databases and registers that are searched.

items.label: Interfaces
items.hint: Through which interface or platform is each database searched, for example Ovid or PubMed?

items.label: Grey literature
items.hint: Sources outside the databases: websites, reports, theses. Or give the reason for doing without.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.hint: The criteria verbatim, with codes, as they apply during screening.

items.label: Search strings
items.hint: The complete search string for each database. Long strings can be attached as a file; then refer to it here.

items.label: Validation of the search
items.hint: How is it checked that the search finds what it should find? For example peer review following PRESS or a test with known papers.

items.label: Other search methods
items.hint: Citation search, hand searching, asking experts.

items.label: Contacting authors
items.hint: Are authors contacted, for instance for full texts or missing information? How often and by what means?

items.label: Results of contacts
items.hint: How are replies and missing replies recorded and reported?

items.label: Validity and repetition of the search
items.hint: When does the search count as out of date, and is it repeated before completion?

items.label: Rationale for the search strategy
items.hint: Why these databases, terms and limits?

items.label: Other search details
items.hint: Anything about the search that fits no other field.

items.label: Screening stages
items.hint: Which stages are there, such as pilot, title/abstract and full text, and what happens in each?

items.label: Visible fields and blinding
items.hint: What information do the screeners see, and do they see the votes of the others?

items.label: Exclusion criteria applied
items.hint: Which criteria apply at which stage, and how are exclusion reasons recorded?

items.label: Instructions for screeners
items.hint: What do the screeners go by? For example criteria with guidance notes and borderline cases. OSF has a field for files here; the protocol can be attached there as well.

items.label: Reliability of screening
items.hint: How many people screen each record, and how is agreement measured? State the threshold in the pilot.

items.label: Resolution of disagreements
items.hint: How are differing votes resolved, and who decides in case of doubt?

items.label: Samples
items.hint: Is only part of the records screened or verified? Size and drawing of the sample.

items.label: Rationale for the approach
items.hint: Why this approach? Refer to the guideline and give reasons for shortcuts.

items.label: Screening data
items.hint: Where are the decisions kept, and what of them is published?

items.label: Other screening details
items.hint: Anything about screening that fits no other field.

items.label: What is extracted
items.hint: The information recorded from each source.

items.label: Extraction stages
items.hint: Pilot and main run; what happens in each stage?

items.label: Instructions for extractors
items.hint: Form with a description for each field, coding rules, examples.

items.label: Blinding during extraction
items.hint: Do the extractors see the others’ entries before they have finished?

items.label: Reliability of extraction
items.hint: Do two people extract independently, or does a second person verify the first person’s entries?

items.label: Resolution during extraction
items.hint: How are differing entries resolved?

items.label: Rationale for the approach
items.hint: Why this approach? Refer to the guideline.

items.label: Extraction data
items.hint: Where are the extracted data kept, and what of them is published?

items.label: Other extraction details
items.hint: Anything about extraction that fits no other field.

items.label: Planned data transformations
items.hint: Is information converted, combined or grouped into categories?

items.label: Missing information
items.hint: How are sources handled that do not report a piece of information?

items.label: Data validation
items.hint: How are the extracted data checked for errors?

items.label: Quality assessment
items.hint: Is methodological quality or risk of bias assessed? With which instrument, or why not?

items.label: Synthesis plan
items.hint: How are the data analysed and presented, for each research question?

items.label: Criteria for conclusions
items.hint: What does the team base its conclusions on? For descriptive reviews “not applicable”, with a reason.

items.label: Blinding during synthesis
items.hint: Are those doing the analysis blinded to anything? Usually “no”.

items.label: Reliability of synthesis
items.hint: How many people do the analysis, and how is it checked?

items.label: Resolution during synthesis
items.hint: How are differing interpretations resolved?

items.label: Publication bias
items.hint: Planned analyses of publication bias, or why there are none.

items.label: Sensitivity analyses
items.hint: Planned checks of whether the results depend on individual decisions, or why there are none.

items.label: Rationale for the approach
items.hint: Why this kind of analysis? Refer to the guideline.

items.label: Synthesis data
items.hint: Where are the analysis and the material kept, and what of them is published?

items.label: Other synthesis details
items.hint: Anything about the synthesis that fits no other field.
